issues.description: The problem statement (and the template Main.java example) define Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters, but the solution introduces a parameter (messageOnRide(String equipment)) in the Rideable interface and its implementations (Pig, Seal). This parameter mismatch breaks the expected method signature and will confuse students: they will implement/expect messageOnRide() with no args (as per UML and Main.java), while the solution shows a different signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) remove the equipment parameter from the solution: change Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and its implementations to messageOnRide() returning the expected string "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement and template (including the UML, Main.java examples, and task descriptions) to document and use messageOnRide(String equipment) so students implement the parameterized variant consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the template usage expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() on Rideable, but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide with a String parameter (messageOnRide(String equipment)) and the implementing classes (Pig, Seal) also implement the method with that parameter. This mismatch in the method signature (same conceptual operation but different parameter lists) creates confusion for students: the UML and sample usage show a no-arg call, whereas the solution requires a parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable.messageOnRide signature across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to use a no-argument method signature (messageOnRide()) and make Pig and Seal implement messageOnRide() accordingly, or (B) update the problem statement and template usage to specify and call messageOnRide(String equipment). Prefer fixing the solution to match the UML/template (no-arg) to avoid changing the exercise specification.
